options: Copying a model's files from one computer to another
A method for compressing a model's file size
Training two models at the same time
The principle that knowledge a model learned on one task can be reused to help it on a different task
questions.explain: Transfer learning is the assumption underneath using any pretrained model: that what it learned generalizes beyond the exact task it was originally trained on.

questions.q: According to the lesson's CNN example, why do a network's early layers tend to generalize well across tasks?
options: Early layers learn simple, broadly useful patterns like edges and textures, which are relevant whether the task is recognizing pets, cars, or anything else
Early layers are always left untrained
Early layers contain the final classification decision
Early layers are larger than later layers
questions.explain: Early CNN layers learn general-purpose features (edges, textures) that are useful for almost any image task, unlike later layers which specialize toward the specific training task.

questions.q: In the lesson's feature-extraction code example, what does setting `param.requires_grad = False` do?
options: It deletes that parameter from the model entirely
It tells backpropagation to skip computing a gradient for that parameter, so it is never updated during training
It doubles the parameter's learning rate
It converts the parameter to a different data type
questions.explain: requires_grad = False excludes a parameter from the chain rule computation, so gradient descent never touches it — it stays frozen at its pretrained value.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked example, roughly what fraction of a ~110-million-parameter base model's parameters does a 1,538-parameter classification head represent?
options: About 50%
About 10%
About 0.0014%
About 100%
questions.explain: 1538 / 110,000,000 is approximately 0.0014%, illustrating how little of the model feature extraction actually trains.

questions.q: How do feature extraction and full fine-tuning relate to each other?
options: They are unrelated techniques with nothing in common
Feature extraction can only be used on images, fine-tuning only on text
Feature extraction always produces better results than fine-tuning
They are two points on the same spectrum of how much of a pretrained model you allow to update, from freezing almost everything to updating everything
questions.explain: Both start from a pretrained model; the difference is how much is frozen versus allowed to update, which is a dial (you can also unfreeze only the later layers) rather than a binary choice.
